standard_prerequisites.name: Additive functors and preservation of direct sums
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma lemma-additive-functor and Lemma lemma-additive-cat-biproduct-kernel
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the characterization of additivity used in the first part and the short exact sequence involving a direct sum.

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 1784-1786): a left or right exact functor preserves finite limits or colimits, hence products or coproducts, hence direct sums, and is therefore additive by the companion characterization.

Part (2) (proof lines 1787-1850): assuming the displayed exactness for short exact sequences, the author uses the short exact sequence involving a direct sum and the induced commutative diagram to show that the functor preserves direct sums, hence is additive, and then derives left exactness; the converse direction is given by the definitions.
Parts (3) and (4) (proof lines 1852-1853): the third statement is the dual of the second, whose proof is written out in the counted span, and the fourth combines the second and the third.
proof_roadmap: Derive additivity from exactness in one direction.
Use the direct sum short exact sequence and the induced diagram for the characterization of left exactness.
Dualize for right exactness and combine for exactness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects characterizations of additive, left exact, right exact and exact functors between abelian categories (statement lines 1761-1781). The proof is a complete argument: additivity of a one-sided exact functor follows from preservation of direct sums and the companion characterization (proof lines 1784-1786); the characterization of left exactness is proved by noting that the displayed exactness makes the functor additive, via the short exact sequence involving a direct sum and the induced commutative diagram, after which left exactness follows (proof lines 1787-1850); the third statement is the dual of the second and the fourth combines the two (proof lines 1852-1853). The non-formal content is the diagram argument for additivity. The claim is H2: a structured argument with the dual parts noted.
